first.rationale: The presenting crisis (competitor entry pricing) points at promotional_pricing, but memory_73 is explicit that promo pricing bought acquisition at the cost of 30-day retention and should not be generalized — that directly conflicts with the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so I am declining the salient move. The two metrics actually degrading are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a single onboarding intervention plausibly moves both; activation_messaging (memory_91) treats the downstream symptom only. Referral incentives (memory_57) work on established customers and do not address the funnel leak; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment than the one under attack. I am spending verification on memory_86 and memory_31 because they are the two load-bearing supports for the action I intend — if the archived records show the lift was small, segment-specific, or measured on a cohort unlike today's, the case collapses and activation_messaging becomes the fallback. Both are also old (day 12 and day 52) and may predate the current funnel. Downstream risk flagged: cutting required signup fields can degrade lead qualification data and starve the demo-request path that memory_44 says produces the best enterprise pipeline, and it may pull in lower-intent accounts that inflate activation while diluting qualified revenue. Guard accordingly — restrict the field-cutting arm to the SMB self-serve path, leave the enterprise demo-request flow untouched, and instrument qualified-revenue and 30/60-day retention, not just completion rate, so we do not repeat the promo-pricing error of optimizing a top-of-funnel number. The prior support here is suggestive, not settled; treat the result as segment-scoped until replicated.

final.rationale: Both verifications came back confirmed, so the action holds. exp_86 is the cleaner of the two: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3% — it improves the funnel without trading away durability, which is exactly what the 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective asks for. exp_31 is also confirmed and carries qualified revenue +4% and activation +9%, but it comes with a small retention dip (-1%) and the record explicitly states it holds on SMB and was not replicated elsewhere. So I weight the onboarding-shortening mechanism as the primary arm and treat signup field-cutting as a secondary, SMB-scoped component rather than a general change. This addresses both degrading metrics with one slot: onboarding completion (-4%) directly, and activation (-6%) via the upstream effect, which is why I still prefer it over activation_messaging (memory_91) treating only the downstream symptom. I continue to decline promotional_pricing despite it being the most obvious answer to the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 is explicit that it damaged 30-day retention and should not be generalized, and buying price-sensitive accounts that churn is the opposite of the objective. referral_incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does not repair the funnel leak; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) serves a segment that is not the one under attack. Risks I am carrying forward and instrumenting: (1) exp_31's evidence is SMB-only and unreplicated, so the field-cutting arm stays confined to the SMB self-serve path and its result is not to be read as a general finding; (2) cutting required signup fields degrades lead-qualification data and could starve the demo-request path that memory_44 identifies as the best enterprise pipeline source, so the enterprise demo-request flow is left untouched; (3) both source records are old (day 12, day 52) and the current funnel may differ, so a replication on today's traffic is part of the point. Success is measured on qualified revenue and 30/60-day retention, not completion or activation alone — the promo-pricing episode is the standing lesson against declaring victory on a top-of-funnel number. If retention moves negative in the SMB arm, kill that component and keep the onboarding-shortening arm.
